body.translated_text: <s>Vṛddhi</s> (strengthened vowels) are <s>ā</s>, <s>ai</s>, and <s>au</s>. || 1.1.1 ||
<s>Guṇa</s> (vowel grades) are <s>a</s>, <s>e</s>, and <s>o</s>. || 1.1.2 ||
<s>Guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> substitute for <s>ik</s> vowels (<s>i</s>, <s>u</s>, <s>ṛ</s>, <s>ḷ</s>). || 1.1.3 ||
There is no elision of the verbal root before an <s>ārdhadhātuka</s> (non-personal) suffix. || 1.1.4 ||
And before suffixes marked with <s>k</s>, <s>ṅ</s>, or having <s>i</s> as <s>it</s> (marker). || 1.1.5 ||
Of <s>dīdhī</s>, <s>vevī</s>, and those with <s>iṭ</s> augment. || 1.1.6 ||
Consonants that are immediately adjacent form a <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunct). || 1.1.7 ||
That which is pronounced through the mouth and nose is <s>anunāsika</s> (nasalized). || 1.1.8 ||
Sounds produced at the same place and with the same effort are <s>savarṇa</s> (homogeneous). || 1.1.9 ||
But not vowels and <s>jhal</s> consonants (hard stops and fricatives) with respect to each other. || 1.1.10 ||
<s>Ī</s>, <s>ū</s>, and <s>e</s> in the dual number are <s>pragṛhya</s> (exempt from sandhi). || 1.1.11 ||
And the <s>māt</s> of the pronoun <s>adas</s>. || 1.1.12 ||
A <s>nipāta</s> (particle) is a word that is monosyllabic or begins with <s>a</s> and ends with a vowel, excluding <s>āṅ</s>. || 1.1.14 ||
In the vocative, according to <s>Śākalya</s>, <s>iti</s> is <s>pragṛhya</s> in non-Vedic usage. || 1.1.16 ||
And <s>ī</s> and <s>ū</s> also when used in the sense of the locative. || 1.1.19 ||
<s>Dā</s> and <s>dhā</s> are called <s>ghu</s>, excluding <s>dāp</s>. || 1.1.20 ||
A single element behaves as if it had both an initial and a final portion. || 1.1.21 ||
<s>Tarap</s> and <s>tamap</s> suffixes are called <s>gha</s>. || 1.1.22 ||
<s>Bahu</s>, <s>gaṇa</s>, words ending in <s>vatu</s>, and <s>ḍati</s> are <s>saṅkhyā</s> (numerals). || 1.1.23 ||
Words ending in <s>ṣṇa</s> are <s>ṣaṭ</s> (a class name). || 1.1.24 ||
<s>Kta</s> and <s>ktavatū</s> are called <s>niṣṭhā</s> (past participle suffixes). || 1.1.26 ||
<s>Sarva</s> and the other words beginning with it are <s>sarvanāman</s> (pronouns). || 1.1.27 ||
Optionally, direction-words and season-words in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. || 1.1.28 ||
Not in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. || 1.1.29 ||
In a compound with the instrumental case. || 1.1.30 ||
And in a <s>dvandva</s> compound. || 1.1.31 ||
Optionally before the <s>jas</s> ending. || 1.1.32 ||
And <s>prathama</s>, <s>carama</s>, <s>taya</s>, <s>alpa</s>, <s>ardha</s>, <s>katipaya</s>, and <s>nema</s>. || 1.1.33 ||
<s>Pūrva</s>, <s>para</s>, <s>avara</s>, <s>dakṣiṇa</s>, <s>uttara</s>, <s>apara</s>, and <s>adhara</s> are pronominal when used in a relative sense, not as proper names. || 1.1.34 ||
<s>Sva</s> (own) is pronominal when not denoting a kinsman's property. || 1.1.35 ||
<s>Antara</s> (inner) is pronominal when meaning an undergarment or outer garment. || 1.1.36 ||
A <s>nipāta</s> (particle) beginning with <s>svar</s> is an <s>avyaya</s> (indeclinable). || 1.1.37 ||
And a <s>taddhita</s> derivative that does not take all case endings. || 1.1.38 ||
And a <s>kṛt</s> derivative ending in <s>m</s> or <s>ej</s>. || 1.1.39 ||
And <s>ktvā</s>, <s>tosun</s>, and <s>kasun</s>. || 1.1.40 ||
And the <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound. || 1.1.41 ||
<s>Śi</s> (the nominative plural ending) marks a <s>sarvanāmasthāna</s> (strong stem position). || 1.1.42 ||
<s>Suṭ</s> augment is added when the stem is not neuter. || 1.1.43 ||
The words <s>na</s> and <s>vā</s> denote <s>vibhāṣā</s> (optionality). || 1.1.44 ||
<s>Ig</s> vowels (<s>i</s>, <s>u</s>, <s>ṛ</s>, <s>ḷ</s>) substituting for <s>yaṇ</s> semivowels are called <s>samprasāraṇa</s>. || 1.1.45 ||
After <s>gāṅ</s> and the <s>kuṭādi</s> class, a suffix not marked with <s>ñ</s>, <s>ṇ</s>, or <s>ṅ</s> as <s>it</s> behaves as <s>ṅit</s>. || 1.2.1 ||
<s>Iṭ</s> augment is added after <s>vij</s>. || 1.2.2 ||
Optionally after <s>ūrṇu</s>. || 1.2.3 ||
A <s>sārvadhātuka</s> (personal) suffix not marked with <s>p</s> as <s>it</s>. || 1.2.4 ||
The <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense) suffix after a root not ending in a conjunct behaves as <s>kit</s>. || 1.2.5 ||
And after <s>indhi</s> and <s>bhavati</s>. || 1.2.6 ||
After <s>mṛḍ</s>, <s>mṛd</s>, <s>gudh</s>, <s>kuṣ</s>, <s>kliś</s>, <s>vad</s>, and <s>vas</s> — the <s>ktvā</s> suffix. || 1.2.7 ||
After <s>rud</s>, <s>vid</s>, <s>muṣ</s>, <s>grah</s>, <s>svap</s>, and <s>pracch</s> — and with <s>sam</s> prefix. || 1.2.8 ||
A <s>jhal</s> consonant replaces the final <s>ik</s> vowel. || 1.2.9 ||
And after a stem ending in a consonant. || 1.2.10 ||
<s>Liṅ</s> and <s>sic</s> take <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) endings. || 1.2.11 ||
Optionally for <s>gam</s>. || 1.2.13 ||
The <s>sic</s> suffix after <s>han</s>. || 1.2.14 ||
<s>Yam</s> in the sense of restraining. || 1.2.15 ||
Optionally in the sense of marrying. || 1.2.16 ||
After <s>sthā</s> and <s>ghu</s> roots, <s>ic</s> is also added. || 1.2.17 ||
Not the <s>ktvā</s> suffix with <s>iṭ</s> augment. || 1.2.18 ||
<s>Niṣṭhā</s> suffixes after <s>śīṅ</s>, <s>svid</s>, <s>mid</s>, <s>kṣvid</s>, and <s>dhṛṣ</s>. || 1.2.19 ||
After <s>mṛṣ</s> in the sense of patient endurance (<s>titikṣā</s>). || 1.2.20 ||
After a root with <s>u</s> as penultimate, optionally in <s>bhāva</s> (abstract) and <s>ādikarman</s> (primary action). || 1.2.21 ||
After <s>pūṅ</s>, and with the <s>ktvā</s> suffix also. || 1.2.22 ||
Optionally, after a root with nasal as penultimate ending in <s>tha</s> or <s>pha</s>. || 1.2.23 ||
And after <s>vañc</s>, <s>luñc</s>, and <s>ṛt</s>. || 1.2.24 ||
After <s>tṛṣ</s>, <s>mṛṣ</s>, and <s>kṛś</s>, according to <s>Kāśyapa</s>. || 1.2.25 ||
After a root with <s>r</s> or <s>l</s> as penultimate, beginning with <s>dhal</s>, and with <s>sam</s> prefix. || 1.2.26 ||
The measure of a vowel (<s>ūkāla</s>) is short, long, or protracted (<s>pluta</s>). || 1.2.27 ||
And of vowels in general. || 1.2.28 ||
A high-pitched vowel is called <s>udātta</s> (acute accent). || 1.2.29 ||
A low-pitched vowel is called <s>anudātta</s> (grave accent). || 1.2.30 ||
A combination of both is called <s>svarita</s> (circumflex accent). || 1.2.31 ||
Of the <s>svarita</s>, the initial portion, half a short mora, is <s>udātta</s>. || 1.2.32 ||
<s>Ekaśruti</s> (monotone) is used when calling from afar and in the vocative. || 1.2.33 ||
In sacrificial rites, in muttered prayers (<s>japa</s>), in the <s>nyūṅkha</s>, and in <s>Sāman</s> chants. || 1.2.34 ||
Optionally, the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is pronounced with a higher pitch. || 1.2.35 ||
Optionally in Vedic usage. || 1.2.36 ||

body.text: na subrahmaṇyāyāṃ svaritasya tu udāttaḥ || PS_1,2.37 ||
body.translated_text: Not in the <s>subrahmaṇyā</s> formula; but the <s>svarita</s> becomes <s>udātta</s>. || 1.2.37 ||
The words <s>deva</s> and <s>brahman</s> are <s>anudātta</s>. || 1.2.38 ||
After a <s>svarita</s>, <s>anudātta</s> syllables in continuous recitation. || 1.2.39 ||
That which follows an <s>udātta</s> or <s>svarita</s> is of a lower pitch (<s>sannatara</s>). || 1.2.40 ||
A suffix consisting of a single sound-unit is called <s>apṛkta</s> (uncompounded). || 1.2.41 ||
A <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound with co-referential terms is called <s>karmadhāraya</s>. || 1.2.42 ||
In a compound, that which is designated in the nominative case is the <s>upasarjana</s> (subordinate member). || 1.2.43 ||
And a single case-ending in a compound not previously enjoined. || 1.2.44 ||
A meaningful element that is neither a verbal root nor a suffix is called a <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem). || 1.2.45 ||
And <s>kṛt</s> derivatives, <s>taddhita</s> derivatives, and compounds. || 1.2.46 ||
The final vowel of a neuter <s>prātipadika</s> is shortened. || 1.2.47 ||
And of <s>go</s> and <s>strī</s> when they are subordinate members. || 1.2.48 ||
<s>Luk</s> elision occurs when there is already <s>luk</s> elision of the <s>taddhita</s> suffix. || 1.2.49 ||
And of <s>id</s> and <s>goṇī</s>. || 1.2.50 ||
When <s>lup</s> elision occurs, the remaining form behaves as if the suffix were present, when expressing a class or individual. || 1.2.51 ||
And of qualifying adjectives, but not when denoting a birth-class. || 1.2.52 ||
That need not be taught, since the technical term itself serves as the authority. || 1.2.53 ||
<s>Lub</s> elision occurs when the combination is not recognized. || 1.2.54 ||
And when the combination serves as the authority, in its absence, there would be non-perception. || 1.2.55 ||
The statement regarding the meaning of the primary suffix applies when the meaning has no other authority. || 1.2.56 ||
And when time is a subordinate element, the treatment is the same. || 1.2.57 ||
When denoting a class-name, the plural may optionally be used for a single entity. || 1.2.58 ||
And the first person pronoun for two referents also. || 1.2.59 ||
And the <s>Phālgunī</s> and <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s> constellations when denoting the asterism. || 1.2.60 ||
In Vedic usage, the singular is used for <s>Punarvasū</s>. || 1.2.61 ||
And for <s>Viśākhā</s>. || 1.2.62 ||

body.text: tiṣya-punarvasvor nakṣatra-dvandve bahuvacanasya dvivacanaṃ nityam || PS_1,2.63 ||
body.translated_text: In a <s>dvandva</s> compound of the constellations <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Punarvasū</s>, the dual invariably replaces the plural. || 1.2.63 ||
Of co-ordinate words with the same ending, there is <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (retention of one) when they share a single case-ending. || 1.2.64 ||

body.text: vṛddho yūnā tal-lakṣaṇaś ced-eva viśeṣaḥ || PS_1,2.65 ||
body.translated_text: An elder is retained over a younger, provided only the distinguishing mark is the same. || 1.2.65 ||
A feminine form is retained like a masculine, and vice versa. || 1.2.66 ||
A masculine is retained over a feminine. || 1.2.67 ||
<s>Bhrātṛ</s> (brother) and <s>putra</s> (son) are retained over <s>svasṛ</s> (sister) and <s>duhitṛ</s> (daughter). || 1.2.68 ||
A neuter is retained with a non-neuter, optionally taking the singular form. || 1.2.69 ||
<s>Pitṛ</s> (father) is retained over <s>mātṛ</s> (mother). || 1.2.70 ||
<s>Śvaśura</s> (father-in-law) is retained over <s>śvaśrū</s> (mother-in-law). || 1.2.71 ||
<s>Tyad</s> and the following demonstrative pronouns are always retained over all others. || 1.2.72 ||
Among village animals in a herd, when not young, the feminine form is retained. || 1.2.73 ||
Roots beginning with <s>bhū</s> are called <s>dhātus</s> (verbal roots). || 1.3.1 ||
In the original teaching, a vowel that is nasal is an <s>it</s> (indicatory marker). || 1.3.2 ||
The final consonant is an <s>it</s>. || 1.3.3 ||
But not the <s>tu</s>, <s>s</s>, or <s>m</s> of a case-ending. || 1.3.4 ||
Initial <s>ñ</s>, <s>ṭu</s>, and <s>ḍu</s> are <s>it</s>. || 1.3.5 ||
<s>Ṣ</s> is an <s>it</s> of a suffix. || 1.3.6 ||
<s>La</s>, <s>śa</s>, and <s>ku</s> are <s>it</s> except in <s>taddhita</s> suffixes. || 1.3.8 ||
The <s>it</s> marker is elided. || 1.3.9 ||
The elaboration of co-ordinate terms follows the order of their enumeration. || 1.3.10 ||
A rule marked with <s>svarita</s> accent is a governing rule (<s>adhikāra</s>). || 1.3.11 ||
A root marked with <s>anudātta</s> accent or <s>ṅ</s> as <s>it</s> takes <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) endings. || 1.3.12 ||
In <s>bhāva</s> (impersonal) and <s>karman</s> (passive) constructions. || 1.3.13 ||
In the active voice when there is reciprocal exchange of actions. || 1.3.14 ||
Not when the meanings are motion or injury. || 1.3.15 ||
And when <s>itaretara</s> or <s>anyonya</s> (mutual) is the accompanying word. || 1.3.16 ||
After <s>ni</s>, the root <s>viś</s> (to enter). || 1.3.17 ||
After <s>pari</s>, <s>vi</s>, and <s>ava</s>, the root <s>kri</s> (to buy). || 1.3.18 ||
After <s>vi</s> and <s>parā</s>, the root <s>ji</s> (to conquer). || 1.3.19 ||
After <s>aṅ</s>, the root <s>dā</s> (to give), not in the sense of cutting or bearing. || 1.3.20 ||
The root <s>krīḍ</s> (to play) after <s>anu</s>, <s>sam</s>, and <s>pari</s> also. || 1.3.21 ||
After <s>sam</s>, <s>ava</s>, <s>pra</s>, and <s>vi</s>, the root <s>sthā</s> (to stand). || 1.3.22 ||
And in the senses of manifesting, abiding, and declaring. || 1.3.23 ||
After <s>ud</s>, the root when the action is not upward. || 1.3.24 ||
After <s>upa</s>, <s>ān</s>, in the sense of performing a mantra-ritual. || 1.3.25 ||
And from an intransitive root. || 1.3.26 ||
After <s>ud</s> and <s>vi</s>, the root <s>tap</s> (to heat). || 1.3.27 ||
After <s>āṅ</s>, the roots <s>yam</s> (to restrain) and <s>han</s> (to strike). || 1.3.28 ||
After <s>sam</s>, the roots <s>gam</s>, <s>ṛcch</s>, <s>pracch</s>, <s>svar</s>, <s>ṛ</s>, <s>śru</s>, and <s>vidigh</s>. || 1.3.29 ||
After <s>ni</s>, <s>sam</s>, <s>upa</s>, and <s>vi</s>, the root <s>hve</s> (to call). || 1.3.30 ||
After <s>āṅ</s>, in the sense of competing. || 1.3.31 ||
The root <s>kṛ</s> (to do) in the senses of injuring, throwing down, serving, acting boldly, endeavoring, declaring, and employing. || 1.3.32 ||
After <s>adhi</s>, in the sense of overpowering. || 1.3.33 ||
After <s>vi</s>, the root whose object is a word (sound). || 1.3.34 ||
And from an intransitive root. || 1.3.35 ||
The root <s>nī</s> (to lead) in the senses of honoring, consigning, performing the teacher's function, knowing, sustaining, disregarding, and spending. || 1.3.36 ||
And when the body, which is the agent's own, is the object. || 1.3.37 ||
The root <s>kram</s> (to step) in the senses of occupying, releasing, and progressing. || 1.3.38 ||
After <s>upa</s> and <s>parā</s>. || 1.3.39 ||
After <s>āṅ</s>, in the sense of ascending. || 1.3.40 ||
After <s>vi</s>, in the sense of moving the feet. || 1.3.41 ||
After <s>pra</s> and <s>upa</s> when they are semantically connected. || 1.3.42 ||
Optionally when without a prefix. || 1.3.43 ||
The root <s>jñā</s> (to know) in the sense of denying. || 1.3.44 ||
And from an intransitive root. || 1.3.45 ||
After <s>sam</s> and <s>prati</s>, not in the sense of studying. || 1.3.46 ||
The root <s>vad</s> (to speak) in the senses of illuminating, conversing, knowing, striving, deliberating, and counseling. || 1.3.47 ||
In the sense of the collective utterance of articulate speakers. || 1.3.48 ||
After <s>anu</s>, from an intransitive root. || 1.3.49 ||
Optionally in the sense of speaking confusedly. || 1.3.50 ||
After <s>ava</s>, the root <s>gṝ</s> (to swallow). || 1.3.51 ||
After <s>sam</s>, in the sense of promising. || 1.3.52 ||
After <s>ud</s>, the root <s>car</s> (to move) when transitive. || 1.3.53 ||
After <s>sam</s>, when accompanied by an instrumental case. || 1.3.54 ||

body.text: dāṇaś ca sā cec caturthy-arthe || PS_1,3.55 ||
body.translated_text: And the root <s>dāṇ</s> also, if a <s>sā</s> suffix is used and if the meaning is that of the dative case. || 1.3.55 ||
After <s>upa</s>, the root <s>yam</s> (to restrain) in the sense of acting on one's own. || 1.3.56 ||
The roots <s>jñā</s>, <s>śru</s>, <s>smṛ</s>, and <s>dṛś</s> with the <s>san</s> (desiderative) suffix. || 1.3.57 ||
But not <s>jñā</s> after <s>anu</s>. || 1.3.58 ||
After <s>prati</s> and <s>āṅ</s>, the root <s>śru</s> (to hear). || 1.3.59 ||
The root <s>śad</s> when marked with <s>śit</s>. || 1.3.60 ||
The root <s>mṛ</s> (to die) in the <s>luṅ</s> (aorist) and <s>liṅ</s> (optative) also. || 1.3.61 ||
The <s>san</s> suffix behaves as previously stated. || 1.3.62 ||
The root <s>kṛ</s> in periphrastic usage behaves like the <s>ām</s> suffix construction. || 1.3.63 ||
After <s>pra</s> and <s>upa</s>, the root <s>yuj</s> (to join), not in the context of sacrificial vessels. || 1.3.64 ||
After <s>sam</s>, the root <s>kṣṇu</s> (to sharpen). || 1.3.65 ||
The root <s>bhuj</s> (to enjoy), not in the sense of bending. || 1.3.66 ||

body.text: ṇe raṇau yat karma ṇau cet sa kartā 'nādhyāne || PS_1,3.67 ||
body.translated_text: When the agent of a causative (<s>ṇi</s>) construction becomes the object, the middle voice is used, not in the sense of studying. || 1.3.67 ||
The roots <s>bhī</s> (to fear) and <s>smi</s> (to smile) when the fear is caused by another. || 1.3.68 ||
The roots <s>gṛdh</s> (to be greedy) and <s>vañc</s> (to deceive) in the sense of cheating. || 1.3.69 ||
The root <s>lī</s> (to cling) in the senses of honoring and making modest also. || 1.3.70 ||
With <s>mithyā</s> (falsely) as an accompanying word, the root <s>kṛ</s> in repeated usage (<s>abhyāsa</s>). || 1.3.71 ||
A root marked with <s>svarita</s> accent or <s>ñit</s> takes middle voice when the result of the action is intended for the agent. || 1.3.72 ||
After <s>apa</s>, the root <s>vad</s> (to speak). || 1.3.73 ||
And the causative (<s>ṇic</s>) suffix. || 1.3.74 ||
After <s>sam</s>, <s>ud</s>, and <s>āṅ</s>, the root <s>yam</s> (to restrain), not in the sense of binding. || 1.3.75 ||
The root <s>jñā</s> without a prefix. || 1.3.76 ||
Optionally when the meaning is understood from the accompanying word. || 1.3.77 ||
For the remaining roots, <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) is used when the agent is the subject. || 1.3.78 ||
After <s>anu</s> and <s>parā</s>, the root <s>kṛ</s> (to do). || 1.3.79 ||
After <s>abhi</s>, <s>prati</s>, and <s>ati</s>, the root <s>kṣip</s> (to throw). || 1.3.80 ||
After <s>pra</s>, the root <s>vah</s> (to carry). || 1.3.81 ||
After <s>pari</s>, the root <s>mṛṣ</s> (to endure). || 1.3.82 ||
After <s>vi</s>, <s>āṅ</s>, and <s>pari</s>, the root <s>ram</s> (to delight). || 1.3.83 ||
And after <s>upa</s>. || 1.3.84 ||
Optionally from an intransitive root. || 1.3.85 ||
After <s>budh</s>, <s>yudh</s>, <s>naś</s>, <s>jan</s>, <s>iṅ</s>, <s>pru</s>, <s>dru</s>, and <s>sru</s>, the <s>ṇe</s> (causative) suffix. || 1.3.86 ||
And from roots meaning swallowing or moving. || 1.3.87 ||
In the <s>aṇ</s> suffix, from an intransitive root when the agent is sentient. || 1.3.88 ||
Not the roots <s>pad</s>, <s>amy-āṅ-yam</s>, <s>āṅ-yas</s>, <s>pari-muh</s>, <s>ruc</s>, <s>nṛt</s>, <s>vad</s>, and <s>vas</s>. || 1.3.89 ||
Optionally the <s>kyaṣ</s> suffix. || 1.3.90 ||
[<s>Ātmanepada</s> is used] after [roots ending in] <s>dh</s> and <s>dbh</s> in <s>luṅ</s> (aorist). || PS_1,3.91 ||
[<s>Ātmanepada</s> is used] after [the root] <s>vṛd</s> and others before <s>sya</s> and <s>san</s>. || PS_1,3.92 ||
And in <s>luṭ</s> (periphrastic future), [<s>ātmanepada</s> is used] after [the root] <s>klup</s>. || PS_1,3.93 ||
Up to [the rule ending with] <s>kaḍāra</s>, [there should be] only one designation [for each item]. || PS_1,4.1 ||
In a conflict of rules, the later rule prevails. || PS_1,4.2 ||
[A feminine stem ending in] <s>ī</s> or <s>ū</s> that denotes a female is [called] <s>nadī</s>. || PS_1,4.3 ||
[But] not [when the <s>ī</s> or <s>ū</s>] is a substitute for <s>iyaṅ</s> or <s>uvaṅ</s>, and not [when it is] non-feminine. || PS_1,4.4 ||
[Nor when the stem ends in] <s>ū</s> before [the case-ending] <s>āmi</s>. || PS_1,4.5 ||
And [a stem ending in a vowel marked with] <s>ṅ</s> [in the <s>Dhātupāṭha</s>], if short, [is not <s>nadī</s>]. || PS_1,4.6 ||
The remainder [of feminine stems not classified as <s>nadī</s>] is [called] <s>ghi</s>, except for <s>sakhi</s>. || PS_1,4.7 ||
<s>Pati</s> [is <s>ghi</s>] only in a compound. || PS_1,4.8 ||
[<s>Pati</s> is <s>ghi</s>] when joined with a genitive case, optionally in Vedic usage. || PS_1,4.9 ||
A short [syllable] is [called] <s>laghu</s> (light). || PS_1,4.10 ||
[A short syllable followed by] a conjunct consonant is [called] <s>guru</s> (heavy). || PS_1,4.11 ||
And a long [syllable is also <s>guru</s>]. || PS_1,4.12 ||
That which begins with the element before which an affix is prescribed is [called] <s>aṅga</s> (base) when an affix [follows]. || PS_1,4.13 ||
That which ends in a <s>sup</s> (nominal ending) or <s>tiṅ</s> (verbal ending) is [called] <s>pada</s> (word). || PS_1,4.14 ||
<s>Na</s> [replaces the final of a <s>pada</s>] before [a suffix beginning with] <s>k</s> or <s>y</s>. || PS_1,4.15 ||
And before [a suffix marked with] <s>s</s>. || PS_1,4.16 ||
Before <s>su</s> and the other [case-endings], when not a <s>sarvanāmasthāna</s> (strong case). || PS_1,4.17 ||
[That portion of a base which stands] before [a suffix beginning with] a vowel (<s>yac</s>) is [called] <s>bha</s>. || PS_1,4.18 ||
[The suffixes] <s>tas</s> and <s>au</s> [take the designation <s>bha</s>] when used in the sense of <s>matup</s> (possessive). || PS_1,4.19 ||
<s>Ayasmaya</s> and the like [are <s>bha</s>] in Vedic usage. || PS_1,4.20 ||
The plural number [is used] for many [entities]. || PS_1,4.21 ||
The dual and singular numbers [are used] for two and one [respectively]. || PS_1,4.22 ||
[The following definitions apply] in the domain of <s>kāraka</s> (case-relations). || PS_1,4.23 ||
The fixed point from which [separation occurs] is [called] <s>apādāna</s> (ablative/source). || PS_1,4.24 ||
[In constructions with verbs meaning] to fear and to protect, the cause of fear [is the <s>apādāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.25 ||
[The <s>apādāna</s> is used] with [the prefixes] <s>parā</s> and <s>ji</s> [in the sense of] that which cannot be endured. || PS_1,4.26 ||
[In constructions with verbs of] warding off, the desired [object is the <s>apādāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.27 ||
In concealment, [the <s>apādāna</s> is] that from which one desires disappearance. || PS_1,4.28 ||
[The <s>apādāna</s> is used] when there is employment of what is communicated. || PS_1,4.29 ||
The original nature of the agent of birth [is the <s>apādāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.30 ||
The source [is the <s>apādāna</s>] of [the root] <s>bhū</s> (to be). || PS_1,4.31 ||

body.text: karmaṇā yam abhipraiti sa sampradānam || PS_1,4.32 ||
body.translated_text: That which the agent intends to reach through the action is [called] <s>sampradāna</s> (dative/recipient). || PS_1,4.32 ||
[With verbs meaning] to please and the like, the one being pleased [is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.33 ||
[With the verbs] <s>ślāgh</s> (to praise), <s>hnuṅ</s> (to hide), <s>sthā</s> (to stand), and <s>śap</s> (to curse), the one intended to be affected [is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.34 ||
[With the root] <s>dhṛ</s> (to owe), the creditor [is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.35 ||
[With the root] <s>spṛh</s> (to desire), the desired [object is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.36 ||

[With verbs meaning] to be angry (<s>krudh</s>), to harm (<s>druh</s>), to envy (<s>īrṣya</s>), and to be indignant (<s>asūya</s>), the one toward whom the anger [is directed is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.37 ||
[With the roots] <s>krudh</s> and <s>druh</s>, when used with a prefix, [the object is the] <s>karma</s> (accusative). || PS_1,4.38 ||
[With the roots] <s>rādh</s> and <s>īkṣ</s>, the one from whom there is inquiry [is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.39 ||
[With the prefixes] <s>prati</s> and <s>āṅ</s> before [the root] <s>śru</s> (to hear), the former agent [is the <s>sampradāna</s>]. || PS_1,4.40 ||
And [with the prefixes] <s>anu</s> and <s>prati</s> before [the root] <s>gṛṇ</s> (to praise). || PS_1,4.41 ||
That which is most effective [in accomplishing the action] is [called] <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument). || PS_1,4.42 ||
[The root] <s>div</s> (to play) [also takes] the <s>karma</s> (accusative). || PS_1,4.43 ||
In [the sense of] price, [the object is] optionally the <s>sampradāna</s>. || PS_1,4.44 ||
The locus is [called] <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (locative). || PS_1,4.45 ||
[With the prefix] <s>adhi</s> before [the roots] <s>śīṅ</s> (to lie), <s>sthā</s> (to stand), and <s>ās</s> (to sit), [the locus is the] <s>karma</s> (accusative). || PS_1,4.46 ||
And [with the root] <s>abhiniviś</s> (to be devoted to). || PS_1,4.47 ||
[With the prefixes] <s>upa</s>, <s>anu</s>, <s>adhi</s>, and <s>āṅ</s> before [the root] <s>vas</s> (to dwell). || PS_1,4.48 ||
That which is most desired by the agent is [called] <s>karma</s> (object/accusative). || PS_1,4.49 ||
And likewise [that which is] connected [with the action but] undesired. || PS_1,4.50 ||
And [that which is] not otherwise mentioned [as any other <s>kāraka</s>]. || PS_1,4.51 ||

The agent of [verbs of] going, knowing, eating, and [verbs denoting] sound, action, and intransitive [verbs] in the <s>aṇi</s> (causative) [becomes the <s>karma</s>]; that same [agent becomes the <s>karma</s>] in the <s>ṇau</s> (causative). || PS_1,4.52 ||
[With the roots] <s>hṛ</s> (to take) and <s>kṛ</s> (to do), optionally [the agent becomes the <s>karma</s> in the causative]. || PS_1,4.53 ||
The independent [entity] is [called] <s>kartṛ</s> (agent). || PS_1,4.54 ||
And the one who causes that [agent to act] is [called] <s>hetu</s> (instigator/causal agent). || PS_1,4.55 ||
[Items defined] before [the sūtra beginning with] <s>rīśvara</s> are [called] <s>nipātas</s> (particles). || PS_1,4.56 ||
<s>Ca</s> (and) and the like [are <s>nipātas</s> when used] in the sense of non-substance. || PS_1,4.57 ||
<s>Pra</s> and the like [are <s>nipātas</s>]. || PS_1,4.58 ||
[<s>Pra</s> and the like are called] <s>upasargas</s> (verbal prefixes) when joined with a verbal action. || PS_1,4.59 ||
And [they are also called] <s>gati</s> (preverb). || PS_1,4.60 ||
And [the terms formed by] <s>ūri</s> and the like, <s>cvi</s>, and <s>ḍāc</s> [are also <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.61 ||
And an onomatopoeia [is <s>gati</s>], provided [the word] <s>iti</s> does not follow. || PS_1,4.62 ||
<s>Sat</s> and <s>asat</s> [are <s>gati</s>] in the senses of respect and disrespect. || PS_1,4.63 ||
<s>Alam</s> [is <s>gati</s>] in the sense of adornment. || PS_1,4.64 ||
<s>Antar</s> [is <s>gati</s>] in the sense of 'not encompassed.' || PS_1,4.65 ||
<s>Kaṇe</s> and <s>manasī</s> [are <s>gati</s>] in the sense of rejection of faith. || PS_1,4.66 ||
<s>Puras</s> (before) is an indeclinable [and a <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.67 ||
And <s>astam</s> (to setting, disappearance) [is an indeclinable and a <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.68 ||
<s>Accha</s> [is a <s>gati</s> when used] with [verbs meaning] motion and speech. || PS_1,4.69 ||
<s>Adas</s> [is a <s>gati</s>] except in the sense of instruction. || PS_1,4.70 ||
<s>Tiras</s> [is a <s>gati</s>] in the sense of concealment. || PS_1,4.71 ||
Optionally [<s>tiras</s> is a <s>gati</s>] with [the root] <s>kṛ</s> (to do). || PS_1,4.72 ||
<s>Upāja</s> and <s>anvāja</s> [are <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.73 ||
And <s>sākṣāt</s> (directly) and those that follow [are also <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.74 ||
<s>Urasi</s> (in the chest) and <s>manasī</s> (in the mind) [are <s>gati</s>] except in the sense of placing upon. || PS_1,4.75 ||
<s>Madhye</s> (in the middle), <s>pade</s> (at the foot), and <s>nivacane</s> [are also <s>gati</s>]. || PS_1,4.76 ||
<s>Haste</s> (in the hand) is always [<s>gati</s>] in the sense of taking a wife's hand in marriage. || PS_1,4.77 ||
<s>Prādhvam</s> [is <s>gati</s>] in the sense of binding. || PS_1,4.78 ||
<s>Jīvikā</s> and <s>upaniṣad</s> [are <s>gati</s>] in the sense of comparison. || PS_1,4.79 ||
These [<s>gatis</s> are placed] before the verbal root. || PS_1,4.80 ||
In Vedic usage, [they may be placed] after [the root] also. || PS_1,4.81 ||
And [they may be] separated [from the root in Vedic usage]. || PS_1,4.82 ||
[The following are called] <s>karmapravacanīyas</s> (case-governing particles). || PS_1,4.83 ||
<s>Anu</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of a characteristic mark. || PS_1,4.84 ||
[<s>Anu</s> is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of the third case (instrumental). || PS_1,4.85 ||
[<s>Anu</s> is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of inferiority. || PS_1,4.86 ||
<s>Upa</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of excess also. || PS_1,4.87 ||
<s>Apa</s> and <s>pari</s> [are <s>karmapravacanīyas</s>] in the sense of exclusion. || PS_1,4.88 ||
<s>Āṅ</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of limit. || PS_1,4.89 ||
<s>Prati</s>, <s>pari</s>, and <s>anu</s> [are <s>karmapravacanīyas</s>] in the senses of a characteristic mark, 'having become so,' designation, portion, and distribution. || PS_1,4.90 ||
<s>Abhi</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of 'not a portion.' || PS_1,4.91 ||
<s>Prati</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the senses of substitute and counter-gift. || PS_1,4.92 ||
<s>Adhi</s> and <s>pari</s> [are <s>karmapravacanīyas</s>] when meaningless. || PS_1,4.93 ||
<s>Su</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of honor. || PS_1,4.94 ||
<s>Ati</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of surpassing. || PS_1,4.95 ||
<s>Api</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the senses of inclusion, possibility, concession, reproach, and combination. || PS_1,4.96 ||
<s>Adhi</s> [is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s>] in the sense of lordship. || PS_1,4.97 ||
Optionally with [the root] <s>kṛ</s> (to do). || PS_1,4.98 ||
<s>La</s> [denotes] <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice endings). || PS_1,4.99 ||
<s>Taṅ</s> and <s>āna</s> [denote] <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice endings). || PS_1,4.100 ||
The <s>tiṅ</s> (verbal endings), in groups of three, are [called] <s>prathama</s> (third person), <s>madhyama</s> (second person), and <s>uttama</s> (first person). || PS_1,4.101 ||
Those, starting from the singular, are singular, dual, and plural, one by one. || PS_1,4.102 ||
[Likewise for] the <s>sup</s> (nominal endings). || PS_1,4.103 ||
And [they are called] <s>vibhakti</s> (case-endings). || PS_1,4.104 ||

body.text: yuṣmady-upapade samāna-adhikaraṇe sthāniny api madhyamaḥ || PS_1,4.105 ||
body.translated_text: When <s>yuṣmad</s> (you) is an accompaniment, co-referential, and standing [in the sentence], the second person [verbal ending is used] even [when the pronoun is not explicitly present]. || PS_1,4.105 ||

body.text: prahāse ca manya-upapade manyater uttama ekavac ca || PS_1,4.106 ||
body.translated_text: In jest, when <s>manya</s> is the accompanying word, the first person singular [is used] with [the root] <s>man</s> (to think). || PS_1,4.106 ||
With <s>asmad</s> (I/we), the first person [ending is used]. || PS_1,4.107 ||
In the remainder [of cases], the third person [ending is used]. || PS_1,4.108 ||
The closest proximity [of sounds] is [called] <s>saṃhitā</s> (euphonic combination). || PS_1,4.109 ||
Cessation [of sound] is [called] <s>avasāna</s> (pause). || PS_1,4.110 ||
[A rule concerning] words [applies only to] those that are syntactically connected. || PS_2,1.1 ||
A <s>sup</s> (case-ending) in the vocative is treated like a subsequent <s>aṅga</s> (base) with respect to accent. || PS_2,1.2 ||
Before [the sūtra ending with] <s>kaḍāra</s>, [the formation described is called] <s>samāsa</s> (compound). || PS_2,1.3 ||
[A compound is formed] together with a <s>sup</s> (declined noun). || PS_2,1.4 ||
[The first type of compound is called] <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable compound). || PS_2,1.5 ||

An indeclinable [forms an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound with a noun] in the senses of case-relation, proximity, abundance, deficiency, absence, transgression, unfitness, sound-manifestation, subsequence, conformity, sequence, simultaneity, similarity, accomplishment, totality, and limit. || PS_2,1.6 ||
<s>Yathā</s> [forms an <s>avyayībhāva</s>] in the sense of similarity. || PS_2,1.7 ||
<s>Yāvat</s> [forms an <s>avyayībhāva</s>] in the sense of specification. || PS_2,1.8 ||
A <s>sup</s> (case-ending) [forms an <s>avyayībhāva</s>] in the sense of 'the measure of' with [the prefix] <s>prati</s>. || PS_2,1.9 ||
<s>Akṣa</s> (dice), <s>śalākā</s> (stick), and numerals [form <s>avyayībhāva</s>] with <s>pari</s>. || PS_2,1.10 ||
Optionally. || PS_2,1.11 ||
<s>Apa</s>, <s>pari</s>, <s>bahis</s>, and <s>añcu</s> derivatives [form <s>avyayībhāva</s>] with the ablative (fifth case). || PS_2,1.12 ||
<s>Āṅ</s> [forms <s>avyayībhāva</s>] in the senses of limit and pervasion. || PS_2,1.13 ||
With <s>abhi</s> and <s>prati</s> [followed by a word denoting] a characteristic mark, [<s>avyayībhāva</s> is formed] in the sense of facing. || PS_2,1.14 ||
<s>Anu</s> [forms <s>avyayībhāva</s>] in the sense of 'following the arrangement of.' || PS_2,1.15 ||
And [<s>anu</s> forms <s>avyayībhāva</s>] with [a noun denoting] that whose length [is specified]. || PS_2,1.16 ||
And <s>tiṣṭhadgu</s> and the like [are also <s>avyayībhāva</s> compounds]. || PS_2,1.17 ||
<s>Pāre</s> (beyond) and <s>madhye</s> (in the middle) [form <s>avyayībhāva</s>], optionally with the genitive (sixth case). || PS_2,1.18 ||
A numeral [forms <s>avyayībhāva</s>] with [a word denoting] lineage. || PS_2,1.19 ||
And with rivers. || PS_2,1.20 ||
And [a compound is formed] in the sense of another word, when it is a proper name. || PS_2,1.21 ||
[The second type of compound is called] <s>tatpuruṣa</s> (determinative compound). || PS_2,1.22 ||
And [the subtype called] <s>dvigu</s> (numeral compound). || PS_2,1.23 ||
The second case (accusative) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound] with [past participles meaning] resorted to, passed, fallen, gone, thrown beyond, reached, and obtained. || PS_2,1.24 ||
[An accusative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with <s>svayam</s> (self) and a <s>kta</s> (past participle). || PS_2,1.25 ||
[The word] <s>khaṭvā</s> (cot) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> with an accusative] in the sense of contempt. || PS_2,1.26 ||
[An accusative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with <s>sāmi</s> (half). || PS_2,1.27 ||
[Accusative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed with] words denoting time. || PS_2,1.28 ||
And in the sense of perpetual connection. || PS_2,1.29 ||
The third case (instrumental) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [a word] expressing a quality that was effected by that [instrument]. || PS_2,1.30 ||
[An instrumental <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with [words meaning] prior, similar, same, inferior, quarrel, skillful, mixed, and smooth. || PS_2,1.31 ||
[An instrumental <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with <s>kartṛ</s> (agent) and <s>karman</s> (object), frequently, when the suffix <s>kta</s> is used. || PS_2,1.32 ||
[An instrumental <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with <s>kṛtya</s> (potential passive participle) suffixes when expressing a comparative sense. || PS_2,1.33 ||
[An instrumental <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed of] a condiment with [the word for] food. || PS_2,1.34 ||
[An instrumental <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed of] mixing with an edible [substance]. || PS_2,1.35 ||
The fourth case (dative) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [words meaning] purpose, benefit, offering, welfare, happiness, and protection. || PS_2,1.36 ||
The fifth case (ablative) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [the word] <s>bhaya</s> (fear). || PS_2,1.37 ||
[An ablative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with [past participles meaning] departed, carried away, released, fallen, and frightened — to a limited extent. || PS_2,1.38 ||

[An ablative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed with] <s>stoka</s> (little), <s>antika</s> (near), <s>dūra</s> (far), <s>artha</s> (meaning), and <s>kṛcchra</s> (difficulty) together with a <s>kta</s> (past participle). || PS_2,1.39 ||
The seventh case (locative) [forms a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [words like] <s>śauṇḍa</s> (drunkard) and the like. || PS_2,1.40 ||
And with [words meaning] completed, dried, cooked, and bound. || PS_2,1.41 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed with the word] <s>dhvāṅkṣa</s> (crow) in the sense of contempt. || PS_2,1.42 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with <s>kṛtya</s> (potential participle) suffixes in the sense of debt. || PS_2,1.43 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] when it is a proper name. || PS_2,1.44 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with a <s>kta</s> (past participle) when [the compound denotes] parts of a day and night. || PS_2,1.45 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed with the word] <s>tatra</s> (there). || PS_2,1.46 ||
[A locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] in the sense of contempt. || PS_2,1.47 ||
And <s>pātrasamita</s> and the like [are locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compounds]. || PS_2,1.48 ||
[Words meaning] former time, one, all, old, ancient, new, and sole [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with a co-referential [word]. || PS_2,1.49 ||
Direction and number [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] when it is a proper name. || PS_2,1.50 ||
And [a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] in the sense of a <s>taddhita</s> affix, a second member, or a collective. || PS_2,1.51 ||
A [compound] preceded by a numeral is [called] <s>dvigu</s>. || PS_2,1.52 ||
[<s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is formed of] censured [things] with words of censure. || PS_2,1.53 ||
<s>Pāpa</s> (wicked) and <s>āṇaka</s> (small) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with censured [words]. || PS_2,1.54 ||
Standards of comparison [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with words denoting a common property. || PS_2,1.55 ||
That which is compared [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with <s>vyāghra</s> (tiger) and the like, when the common property is not separately expressed. || PS_2,1.56 ||
A qualifier [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with the qualified, frequently. || PS_2,1.57 ||

And [the words] <s>pūrva</s> (prior), <s>apara</s> (later), <s>prathama</s> (first), <s>carama</s> (last), <s>jaghanya</s> (lowest), <s>samāna</s> (same), <s>madhya</s> (middle), <s>madhyama</s> (middlemost), and <s>vīra</s> (heroic) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s> with the qualified]. || PS_2,1.58 ||
<s>Śreṇī</s> (row) and the like [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with <s>kṛta</s> (made) and the like. || PS_2,1.59 ||
[A <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with a <s>kta</s> (past participle) qualified by <s>nañ</s> (negative), when [the first member] is not <s>nañ</s>. || PS_2,1.60 ||

[The words] <s>sat</s> (good), <s>mahat</s> (great), <s>parama</s> (supreme), <s>uttama</s> (best), and <s>utkṛṣṭa</s> (excellent) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with words denoting the honored one. || PS_2,1.61 ||
<s>Vṛndāraka</s> (chief), <s>nāga</s> (elephant), and <s>kuñjara</s> (elephant) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [a word denoting] the one being honored. || PS_2,1.62 ||
<s>Katara</s> (which of two) and <s>katama</s> (which of many) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] in a question about class or species. || PS_2,1.63 ||
<s>Kim</s> (what) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] in the sense of contempt. || PS_2,1.64 ||

<s>Poṭā</s> (mare), <s>yuvati</s> (young woman), <s>stoka</s> (small), <s>katipaya</s> (some), <s>gṛṣṭi</s> (cow that has calved once), <s>dhenu</s> (milch-cow), <s>vaśā</s> (barren cow), <s>vehad</s>, <s>baṣkayaṇī</s> (young cow), <s>pravaktṛ</s> (teacher), <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in the <s>Vedas</s>), <s>adhyāpaka</s> (instructor), and <s>dhūrta</s> (rogue) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s> with a word denoting] class or species. || PS_2,1.65 ||
And with words of praise. || PS_2,1.66 ||
<s>Yuvan</s> (young) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with <s>khalati</s> (bald), <s>pālita</s> (grey-haired), <s>valina</s> (wrinkled), and <s>jaratī</s> (old woman). || PS_2,1.67 ||
<s>Kṛtya</s> (potential participle), <s>tulya</s> (equal), and <s>ākhyā</s> (designation) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>], not [with a word denoting] class. || PS_2,1.68 ||
[A word denoting] color [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [another word denoting] color. || PS_2,1.69 ||
<s>Kumāra</s> (youth) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with <s>śramaṇā</s> (female ascetic) and the like. || PS_2,1.70 ||
[The word] <s>catuṣpāda</s> (four-footed) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with <s>garbhiṇī</s> (pregnant). || PS_2,1.71 ||
And <s>mayūravyaṃsaka</s> and the like [are <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compounds]. || PS_2,1.72 ||
<s>Pūrva</s> (east), <s>apara</s> (west), <s>adhara</s> (south), and <s>uttara</s> (north) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with [a word denoting] a part of a whole, when there is co-reference. || PS_2,2.1 ||
<s>Ardha</s> (half) [is compounded as] neuter. || PS_2,2.2 ||
[The words] <s>dvitīya</s> (second), <s>tṛtīya</s> (third), <s>caturtha</s> (fourth), and <s>turya</s> (quarter) [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>], optionally. || PS_2,2.3 ||
And [the words meaning] obtained and arrived [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with the accusative (second case). || PS_2,2.4 ||
Words denoting time [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>] with a word denoting measure. || PS_2,2.5 ||
<s>Nañ</s> (negative particle) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>]. || PS_2,2.6 ||
[<s>Nañ</s> forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s> in the senses of] slightly and not done. || PS_2,2.7 ||
The sixth case (genitive) [forms <s>tatpuruṣa</s>]. || PS_2,2.8 ||
And with <s>yājaka</s> (officiating priest) and the like. || PS_2,2.9 ||
Not in the sense of partitive (selection from a group). || PS_2,2.10 ||
[A genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with [words denoting] ordinal, quality, beneficial, purpose, good, indeclinable, <s>tavya</s> (potential suffix), when co-referential. || PS_2,2.11 ||
And with a <s>kta</s> (past participle) in the sense of honor. || PS_2,2.12 ||
And with a word denoting a location (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). || PS_2,2.13 ||
And [a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with [a word denoting the] object (<s>karman</s>). || PS_2,2.14 ||
With [the suffixes] <s>tṛc</s> and <s>aka</s> [denoting] the agent. || PS_2,2.15 ||
And [a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] with [a word denoting] the agent. || PS_2,2.16 ||
Always [genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is formed] in the senses of play and livelihood. || PS_2,2.17 ||
<s>Ku</s> (bad), <s>gati</s> (preverb), <s>pra</s>, and the like [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compounds]. || PS_2,2.18 ||
A governing word (<s>upapada</s>) [forms a compound], not being a finite verb (<s>tiṅ</s>). || PS_2,2.19 ||
<s>Amā</s> and <s>eva</s> [form compounds] with an indeclinable. || PS_2,2.20 ||
[Words in] the third case and those that follow [form <s>tatpuruṣa</s>], optionally. || PS_2,2.21 ||
And [a compound is formed] with [the absolutive suffix] <s>ktvā</s>. || PS_2,2.22 ||
The remainder is <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (exocentric compound). || 2.2.23 ||
Multiple [words are compounded] when the meaning refers to another word. || 2.2.24 ||
A numeral [compounds] with <s>avyaya</s> (indeclinable), near, not far, greater, or [another] numeral, when referring to something countable. || 2.2.25 ||
Direction-names [compound] when [they denote] an intermediate [direction]. || 2.2.26 ||
'That which is there or of that' [compounds] when the forms are identical. || 2.2.27 ||
'Together with that' [compounds] when denoting co-participation. || 2.2.28 ||
In the sense of 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [the compound is called] <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). || 2.2.29 ||
The subordinate member (<s>upasarjana</s>) comes first. || 2.2.30 ||
In [compounds such as] <s>rājadanta</s> and the like, it comes last. || 2.2.31 ||
In a <s>dvandva</s>, the <s>ghi</s>-[ending stem comes first]. || 2.2.32 ||
[The member] beginning with a vowel and ending in a short vowel [comes first]. || 2.2.33 ||
[The member with] fewer vowels [comes first]. || 2.2.34 ||
A seventh-case (locative) qualifier [comes first] in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. || 2.2.35 ||
[Also] a <s>niṣṭhā</s> (past participle) [comes first in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>]. || 2.2.36 ||
Optionally in [compounds beginning with] <s>āhitāgni</s> and the like. || 2.2.37 ||
<s>Kaḍāra</s>-[ending words come first] in a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound). || 2.2.38 ||
When [the <s>kāraka</s> relation] is not expressed [by other means]. || 2.3.1 ||
The second case (accusative) [is used] for the object (<s>karman</s>). || 2.3.2 ||
And the third case (instrumental) [replaces the accusative] for <s>hoḥ</s> in Vedic usage. || 2.3.3 ||
[The accusative is used] when joined with <s>antarā</s> or <s>antareṇa</s> ('between'). || 2.3.4 ||
[The accusative is used] for [denoting] continuous connection with time or distance. || 2.3.5 ||
The third case (instrumental) [is used] for completion (<s>apavarga</s>). || 2.3.6 ||
The seventh (locative) and fifth (ablative) [are used] in the middle of <s>kārakas</s>. || 2.3.7 ||
The second case (accusative) [is used] when joined with a <s>karmapravacanīya</s> (pre-verb). || 2.3.8 ||

body.text: yasmād adhikaṃ yasya ca+īśvara-vacanaṃ tatra saptamī || PS_2,3.9 ||
body.translated_text: The seventh case (locative) [is used] in the sense of 'that from which there is excess' and 'one who has power over.' || 2.3.9 ||
[Also] the fifth case (ablative) [is used] with <s>apa</s>, <s>āṅ</s>, and <s>pari</s>. || 2.3.10 ||
And [the fifth case is used] for the source in [the sense of] substitute and reciprocal giving. || 2.3.11 ||
The second (accusative) and fourth (dative) [are used] for the object of a verb of motion, in an action, when not referring to a path. || 2.3.12 ||
The fourth case (dative) [is used] for the recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>). || 2.3.13 ||
And [the dative is used] for the object of a verb when the subordinate word denotes the purpose of an action, [when the agent] is a stationary [entity]. || 2.3.14 ||
And [the dative is used] after a word denoting action in the sense of <s>tum</s> (infinitive purpose). || 2.3.15 ||
And [the dative is used] when connected with <s>namaḥ</s> ('homage'), <s>svasti</s> ('welfare'), <s>svāhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, <s>alam</s> ('enough'), and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>. || 2.3.16 ||
Optionally [the dative is used] for the object of <s>manya</s> (to think) in the sense of disrespect, when not referring to living beings. || 2.3.17 ||
The third case (instrumental) [is used] for the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) and the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). || 2.3.18 ||
[The instrumental is used] for the non-principal [element] when joined with <s>saha</s> ('together with'). || 2.3.19 ||
[The instrumental is used for] that by which [there is] a bodily deformity. || 2.3.20 ||
[The instrumental is used] as a characteristic of 'being in such a state.' || 2.3.21 ||
Optionally [the instrumental is used] for the object of <s>sañjña</s> (to designate). || 2.3.22 ||
[The instrumental is used] in the sense of cause (<s>hetu</s>). || 2.3.23 ||
The fifth case (ablative) [is used] for a debt (<s>ṛṇa</s>) when not [referring to] the agent. || 2.3.24 ||
Optionally [the ablative is used] for a quality, when not feminine. || 2.3.25 ||
The sixth case (genitive) [is used] when a cause is employed. || 2.3.26 ||
And the third case (instrumental) [is used] for a pronoun. || 2.3.27 ||
The fifth case (ablative) [is used] for the point of departure (<s>apādāna</s>). || 2.3.28 ||

[The ablative is used] when joined with <s>anya</s> ('other'), <s>ārāt</s> ('far'), <s>itara</s> ('another'), <s>ṛte</s> ('without'), direction-words, <s>añcu</s>-[ending words], and <s>uttarapada</s>s [ending in] vowels. || 2.3.29 ||
The sixth case (genitive) [is used] with a suffix in the sense of <s>atas</s>. || 2.3.30 ||
The second case (accusative) [is used] with <s>enapā</s>. || 2.3.31 ||
Optionally the third case (instrumental) [is used] with <s>pṛthak</s> ('separately'), <s>vinā</s> ('without'), and <s>nānā</s> ('variously'). || 2.3.32 ||

And [the instrumental is used] with <s>kareṇa</s> for <s>stoka</s> ('a little'), <s>alpa</s> ('small'), <s>kṛcchra</s> ('with difficulty'), and <s>katipaya</s> ('some'), when denoting something without substance. || 2.3.33 ||
Optionally the sixth case (genitive) [is used] with words meaning 'far' and 'near.' || 2.3.34 ||
And the second case (accusative) [is used] with words meaning 'far' and 'near.' || 2.3.35 ||
And the seventh case (locative) [is used] for the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). || 2.3.36 ||
[The locative is used for] that whose state is characterized by the state of another. || 2.3.37 ||
And the sixth case (genitive) [is used] in the sense of disrespect. || 2.3.38 ||

And [the genitive is used] with <s>svāmin</s> ('owner'), <s>īśvara</s> ('lord'), <s>adhipati</s> ('ruler'), <s>dāyāda</s> ('heir'), <s>sākṣin</s> ('witness'), <s>pratibhū</s> ('surety'), and <s>prasūta</s> ('born of'). || 2.3.39 ||
And [the genitive is used] with <s>āyukta</s> ('appointed') and <s>kuśala</s> ('skilled') in the sense of devoted practice. || 2.3.40 ||
And [the genitive is used for] that from which there is selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). || 2.3.41 ||
The fifth case (ablative) [is used] when there is a partition. || 2.3.42 ||
The seventh case (locative) [is used] with <s>sādhu</s> ('good at') and <s>nipuṇa</s> ('skilled') in the sense of respectful skill, not [being a prefix] <s>prati</s>. || 2.3.43 ||
And the third case (instrumental) [is used] with <s>prasita</s> ('devoted') and <s>utsuka</s> ('eager'). || 2.3.44 ||
And [the locative is used] for a <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) when there is elision (<s>lup</s>). || 2.3.45 ||
The first case (nominative) [is used] merely for expressing the meaning of the nominal stem, gender, and measure. || 2.3.46 ||
And [the first case is used] in address (<s>sambodhana</s>). || 2.3.47 ||
That [first case in address] is called <s>āmantrita</s> (vocative). || 2.3.48 ||
The singular [of the vocative] is called <s>sambuddhi</s>. || 2.3.49 ||
The sixth case (genitive) [is used] for the remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>). || 2.3.50 ||
Of <s>jña</s> (to know) in the sense of <s>avid</s> (not knowing), [the genitive is used] for the instrument. || 2.3.51 ||
[The genitive is used] for the object of <s>adhi</s>+<s>i</s> (to study), <s>artha</s> (to request), <s>dayā</s> (to pity), and <s>īś</s> (to rule). || 2.3.52 ||
Of <s>kṛñ</s> (to do), [the genitive is used] for a repeated effort. || 2.3.53 ||
Of [verbs meaning] pain (<s>rujā</s>), [the genitive is used] for words denoting a state, except <s>jvara</s> (fever). || 2.3.54 ||
[The genitive is used for] <s>nātha</s> (to implore) in the sense of a blessing. || 2.3.55 ||
[The genitive is used for] <s>jāsi</s>, <s>ni-prahaṇa</s>, <s>nāṭa</s>, <s>krātha</s>, and <s>piṣ</s> in the sense of harming. || 2.3.56 ||
[The genitive is used for] <s>vyavahṛ</s> (to deal) and <s>paṇ</s> (to wager) when both [parties] are involved. || 2.3.57 ||
[The genitive is used for] <s>div</s> (to play) when [used] for its own purpose. || 2.3.58 ||
Optionally [the genitive is used] when there is a prefix (<s>upasarga</s>). || 2.3.59 ||
The second case (accusative) [is used] in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts]. || 2.3.60 ||
Of <s>preṣya</s> (to command) and <s>brū</s> (to speak), [the dative is used] for <s>havis</s> (oblation) when the deity is the recipient. || 2.3.61 ||
Frequently [the fourth case is used] in the sense of the fourth case in Vedic usage. || 2.3.62 ||
And [the genitive is used] for the instrument of <s>yaj</s> (to sacrifice). || 2.3.63 ||
[The locative is used] for time as locus when <s>kṛtva</s>-meaning is employed. || 2.3.64 ||
[The sixth case is used] for the agent and object in [a construction with] a <s>kṛt</s> (primary derivative) suffix. || 2.3.65 ||
When both [agent and object] are applicable, [the sixth case is used] for the object. || 2.3.66 ||
And [the sixth case is used] for <s>kta</s> (past participle) in the present [sense]. || 2.3.67 ||
And [the sixth case is used] for a word denoting a locus. || 2.3.68 ||
[The above rule] does not [apply to suffixes] <s>la</s>, <s>u</s>, <s>uka</s>, <s>avyaya</s> (indeclinables), <s>niṣṭhā</s>, <s>khalarthaḥ</s>, and <s>tṛn</s>. || 2.3.69 ||
Of <s>aka</s> and <s>in</s> [suffixes], [the sixth case is used] for a future [action] and indebtedness. || 2.3.70 ||
Of <s>kṛtya</s> (gerundive) [suffixes], optionally [the sixth case is used] for the agent. || 2.3.71 ||
Optionally the third case (instrumental) [is used] with words meaning 'equal,' except <s>tulā</s> and <s>upamā</s>. || 2.3.72 ||

And the fourth case (dative) [is used] in blessings with <s>āyuṣya</s> ('long-lived'), <s>madra</s>, <s>bhadra</s> ('auspicious'), <s>kuśala</s> ('well'), <s>sukha</s> ('happy'), <s>artha</s> ('benefit'), and <s>hita</s> ('good'). || 2.3.73 ||
A <s>dvigu</s> (numeral compound) [takes] singular number. || 2.4.1 ||
And a <s>dvandva</s> [takes singular] for living beings, musical instruments, army divisions, and body parts. || 2.4.2 ||
[Singular <s>dvandva</s> is used] in recitation for [Vedic] schools (<s>caraṇas</s>). || 2.4.3 ||
<s>Adhvaryu-kratu</s> [compounds are] not neuter. || 2.4.4 ||
Of those whose names are not remote, [singular is used] when [referring to] study-based [lineages]. || 2.4.5 ||
The class (<s>jāti</s>) [is denoted] for non-living things. || 2.4.6 ||
A river and a country with a specific gender [take that gender], except villages. || 2.4.7 ||
[Singular <s>dvandva</s> is used for] small creatures. || 2.4.8 ||
And [for those groups] whose mutual opposition is perpetual. || 2.4.9 ||
Of <s>Śūdras</s> who have not completed [their ceremonies]. || 2.4.10 ||
And [compounds] beginning with <s>gavāśva</s> ('cows and horses'). || 2.4.11 ||
Optionally for trees, animals, grasses, grains, condiments, domestic animals, birds, horses-and-mares, and front-back/lower-upper [pairs]. || 2.4.12 ||
A contradictory [<s>dvandva</s>], when it does not denote a locus, [is neuter singular]. || 2.4.13 ||
Not [for compounds such as] <s>dadhipaya</s> ('curd and milk') and the like. || 2.4.14 ||
And when [the <s>dvandva</s> denotes] a locus and [its] extent. || 2.4.15 ||
Optionally [neuter singular] in the sense of proximity. || 2.4.16 ||
That [<s>samāhāra dvandva</s>] is neuter. || 2.4.17 ||
And [so is] the <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable compound). || 2.4.18 ||
A <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [formed with] <s>nañ</s> (negative) [or being a] <s>karmadhāraya</s> [takes the gender of the latter member]. || 2.4.19 ||
In proper names, [the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> takes the feminine gender] with <s>kantā</s>, among the <s>Uśīnaras</s>. || 2.4.20 ||
<s>Upajñā</s> (originator) and <s>upakrama</s> (initiator) [come first] when one wishes to indicate that [person] as the first. || 2.4.21 ||
<s>Chāyā</s> (shadow/image) [takes feminine gender] when used frequently. || 2.4.22 ||
<s>Sabhā</s> (assembly) and <s>rājan</s> (king) [take masculine gender] when not preceded by a non-human [word]. || 2.4.23 ||
And <s>aśālā</s> [takes the gender of the latter member]. || 2.4.24 ||
Optionally for <s>senā</s>, <s>surā</s>, <s>chāyā</s>, <s>śālā</s>, and <s>niśā</s>. || 2.4.25 ||
In <s>dvandva</s> and <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compounds], the gender [follows] the latter member. || 2.4.26 ||
<s>Aśva</s> and <s>vaḍavā</s> [follow] the same rule as before. || 2.4.27 ||
<s>Hemanta-śiśira</s> ('winter pair') and <s>aho-rātra</s> ('day-and-night') [take special forms] in Vedic usage. || 2.4.28 ||
<s>Rātra</s>, <s>ahna</s>, and <s>ahāḥ</s> are masculine. || 2.4.29 ||
<s>Apatha</s> ('non-road') is neuter. || 2.4.30 ||
And <s>ardharca</s> ('half-verse') is masculine. || 2.4.31 ||
Of <s>idam</s> ('this'), in subsequent reference, <s>aś</s> [is the substitute], unaccented, in the third case and onward. || 2.4.32 ||

body.text: etadas tra-tasos tra-tasau ca anudātau || PS_2,4.33 ||
body.translated_text: Of <s>etad</s> ('that'), <s>tra</s> and <s>tas</s> [replace] <s>tra</s> and <s>tas</s>, and [are] unaccented. || 2.4.33 ||
In the second case and in <s>ṭā</s> and <s>os</s>, <s>ena</s> [is the substitute]. || 2.4.34 ||
[The following substitutions apply] in an <s>ārdhadhātuka</s> (non-<s>sārvadhātuka</s>) [suffix environment]. || 2.4.35 ||

body.text: ado jagdhir lyap ti kiti || PS_2,4.36 ||
body.translated_text: Of <s>ad</s> ('to eat'), <s>jagdhi</s> [is the substitute before] <s>lyap</s>, <s>ti</s>, and [suffixes marked with] <s>kit</s>. || 2.4.36 ||
Of <s>luṅ</s> (aorist) and <s>san</s> (desiderative), <s>ghas</s> [is the substitute with <s>lṛ</s>]. || 2.4.37 ||
And [<s>ghas</s> is the substitute] before <s>ghañ</s> and <s>ap</s> [suffixes]. || 2.4.38 ||
Variously in Vedic usage. || 2.4.39 ||
Optionally in <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense). || 2.4.40 ||
Of <s>ve</s> (to weave), <s>vayi</s> [is the substitute]. || 2.4.41 ||
Of <s>han</s> (to kill), <s>vadha</s> [is the substitute] in <s>liṅ</s> (optative). || 2.4.42 ||
And in <s>luṅ</s> (aorist). || 2.4.43 ||
Optionally in <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) [endings]. || 2.4.44 ||
Of <s>iṇ</s> (to go), <s>gā</s> [is the substitute] in <s>luṅ</s> (aorist). || 2.4.45 ||
In <s>ṇi</s> (causative), <s>gam</s> [is the substitute for <s>i</s>] except in the sense of understanding. || 2.4.46 ||
And in <s>san</s> (desiderative). || 2.4.47 ||
And of <s>iṅ</s> [root]. || 2.4.48 ||
<s>Gāṅ</s> [is the substitute] in <s>liṭ</s> (perfect). || 2.4.49 ||
Optionally in <s>luṅ</s> (aorist) and <s>lṛṅ</s> (conditional). || 2.4.50 ||
And in <s>ṇi</s> (causative) with <s>sam</s> and <s>caṅ</s> (intensive). || 2.4.51 ||
Of <s>as</s> (to be), <s>bhū</s> [is the substitute]. || 2.4.52 ||
Of <s>brū</s> (to speak), <s>vac</s> [is the substitute]. || 2.4.53 ||
Of <s>cakṣiṅ</s> (to see), <s>khyāñ</s> [is the substitute]. || 2.4.54 ||
Optionally in <s>liṭ</s> (perfect). || 2.4.55 ||
Of <s>aj</s> (to drive), <s>vi</s> [is the substitute] except before <s>ghañ</s> and <s>ap</s>. || 2.4.56 ||
Optionally before <s>yau</s>. || 2.4.57 ||

Of [a suffix denoting one] belonging to the <s>ṇya</s>-class, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>ṛṣi</s>-lineage, or [a suffix] marked with <s>ñit</s> — for a young person, there is elision of <s>aṇ</s> and <s>iñ</s>. || 2.4.58 ||
And from <s>Paila</s> and the like. || 2.4.59 ||
Of <s>iñ</s>, [there is elision] according to the eastern [grammarians]. || 2.4.60 ||
Not from the <s>Taulvali</s>-class. || 2.4.61 ||
Of the <s>tadrāja</s> (royal dynasty) [suffix], when [denoting] many, [it is replaced] by that very [word], when not feminine. || 2.4.62 ||
From <s>Yaska</s> and the like, in <s>gotra</s> (family lineage). || 2.4.63 ||
And of <s>yañ</s> and <s>añ</s>. || 2.4.64 ||
And from <s>Atri</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Kutsa</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gotama</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. || 2.4.65 ||
Of a polysyllabic <s>iñ</s>-[derivative], among the eastern <s>Bharatas</s>. || 2.4.66 ||
Not from <s>Gopavana</s> and the like. || 2.4.67 ||
From <s>Tika</s>, <s>Kitava</s>, and the like, in a <s>dvandva</s>. || 2.4.68 ||
From <s>Upaka</s> and the like, optionally, when not a <s>dvandva</s>. || 2.4.69 ||
For <s>Āgastya</s> and <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, [the substitutes are] <s>Agasti</s> and <s>Kuṇḍinac</s>. || 2.4.70 ||
The case-endings (<s>sup</s>) [are elided] for verbal roots (<s>dhātu</s>) and nominal stems (<s>prātipadika</s>). || 2.4.71 ||
Of <s>śap</s> (vikaraṇa), [there is elision] after <s>ad</s>-class roots and the like. || 2.4.72 ||
Variously in Vedic usage. || 2.4.73 ||
And of <s>yaṅ</s> (intensive), before a vowel. || 2.4.74 ||
From <s>juhotyādi</s> (the <s>hu</s>-class) and the like, <s>ślu</s> [is the elision of <s>śap</s>]. || 2.4.75 ||
Variously in Vedic usage. || 2.4.76 ||
Of <s>sic</s> (aorist sign), [there is elision] after <s>gāti</s>, <s>sthā</s>, <s>ghu</s>-[roots], <s>pā</s>, and <s>bhū</s>, in <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice). || 2.4.77 ||
Optionally [the elision of <s>sic</s> occurs] after <s>ghrā</s>, <s>dheṭ</s>, <s>śā</s>, <s>chā</s>, and <s>sa</s>. || 2.4.78 ||
Of <s>ta</s> and <s>thās</s> [endings], [there is elision] after <s>tan</s>-class roots and the like. || 2.4.79 ||

In Vedic mantras, of <s>le</s> [ending], [there is substitution] after <s>ghas</s>, <s>hvṛ</s>, <s>naś</s>, <s>vṛ</s>, <s>dah</s>, <s>ād</s>, <s>vṛc</s>, <s>kṛ</s>, <s>gam</s>, and <s>jan</s>. || 2.4.80 ||
[And there is substitution of] <s>ām</s>. || 2.4.81 ||
After an indeclinable, [there is elision] of <s>āp</s> and <s>sup</s> (case endings). || 2.4.82 ||

body.text: na avyayībhāvād ato 'm tv apañcamyāḥ || PS_2,4.83 ||
body.translated_text: Not [the elision] of <s>am</s> after an <s>avyayībhāva</s> ending in <s>a</s>, except in the fifth case. || 2.4.83 ||
In the third and seventh cases, variously. || 2.4.84 ||
Of <s>luṭ</s> (periphrastic future), for the first person, <s>ḍā</s>, <s>rau</s>, and <s>ras</s> [are the endings]. || 2.4.85 ||
[A word that follows a base is called] a suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>). || 3.1.1 ||
And [the suffix comes] after [the base]. || 3.1.2 ||
And [the suffix has] an acute accent on the first [syllable]. || 3.1.3 ||
<s>Sup</s> (nominal endings) and [suffixes] marked with <s>pit</s> are unaccented. || 3.1.4 ||
After <s>gup</s> (to protect), <s>tij</s> (to be sharp), and <s>kit</s> (to cure), [the suffix] <s>san</s> (desiderative) [is added]. || 3.1.5 ||
After <s>mān</s>, <s>badh</s>, <s>dān</s>, and <s>śān</s>, the reduplication syllable is lengthened. || 3.1.6 ||

body.text: dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samāna-kartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā || PS_3,1.7 ||
body.translated_text: After a verbal root, [<s>san</s> is added] for the object, when the agent is the same, optionally in the sense of desire. || 3.1.7 ||
After a nominal stem (<s>sup</s>), <s>kyac</s> [is added] for oneself. || 3.1.8 ||
And <s>kāmyac</s> [is added]. || 3.1.9 ||
After a standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), [<s>kyac</s> is added] in the sense of behaving like. || 3.1.10 ||
Of the agent, <s>kyaṅ</s> [is added], with elision of the <s>s</s>. || 3.1.11 ||

body.text: bhṛśādibhyo bhuvy-acver lopaś ca halaḥ || PS_3,1.12 ||
body.translated_text: After <s>bhṛśa</s> and the like, <s>bhuv</s> and <s>acv</s> [are added], with elision of the consonant. || 3.1.12 ||
After <s>lohita</s> and similar [words formed with] <s>ḍāc</s>, <s>kyaṣ</s> [is added]. || 3.1.13 ||
[<s>Kyaṣ</s> is added to] <s>kaṣṭa</s> in the sense of going through [difficulty]. || 3.1.14 ||
For the object, [denominative suffixes are added] from <s>romantha</s> ('rumination') and <s>tapas</s> ('austerity'), with <s>vart</s> and <s>car</s>. || 3.1.15 ||
From <s>bāṣpa</s> ('tears') and <s>ūṣma</s> ('heat'), in the sense of emitting. || 3.1.16 ||
From <s>śabda</s> ('sound'), <s>vaira</s> ('enmity'), <s>kalaha</s> ('quarrel'), <s>abhra</s> ('cloud'), <s>kaṇva</s>, and <s>megha</s> ('cloud'), in the sense of producing. || 3.1.17 ||
From <s>sukha</s> ('happiness') and the like, when the agent [himself] experiences [the state]. || 3.1.18 ||
From <s>namaḥ</s>, <s>varivas</s>, and <s>citraṅ</s>, <s>kyac</s> [is added]. || 3.1.19 ||
From <s>puccha</s> ('tail'), <s>bhāṇḍa</s> ('vessel'), and <s>cīvara</s> ('robe'), <s>ṇiṅ</s> [is added]. || 3.1.20 ||

From <s>muṇḍa</s> ('shaved'), <s>miśra</s> ('mixed'), <s>ślakṣṇa</s> ('smooth'), <s>lavaṇa</s> ('salt'), <s>vrata</s> ('vow'), <s>vastra</s> ('cloth'), <s>hala</s> ('plough'), <s>kala</s> ('soft'), <s>kṛta</s> ('done'), and <s>tūsta</s>, <s>ṇic</s> (causative) [is added]. || 3.1.21 ||

body.text: dhātor eka-aco hala-ādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ || PS_3,1.22 ||
body.translated_text: After a monosyllabic verbal root beginning with a consonant, <s>yaṅ</s> (intensive) [is added] in the sense of repetition or intensity of action. || 3.1.22 ||
Always [<s>yaṅ</s> is added for] crooked movement in the sense of going. || 3.1.23 ||
From the roots <s>lup</s>, <s>sad</s>, <s>car</s>, <s>jap</s>, <s>jabh</s>, <s>dah</s>, <s>daś</s>, and <s>gṝ</s>, [the affix <s>ṇic</s> is added] in the sense of censure of the action.

The affix <s>ṇic</s> [is added] after <s>satyāpa</s>, <s>pāśa</s>, <s>rūpa</s>, <s>vīṇā</s>, <s>tūla</s>, <s>śloka</s>, <s>senā</s>, <s>loma</s>, <s>tvaca</s>, <s>varma</s>, <s>varṇa</s>, <s>cūrṇa</s>, and roots of the <s>curādi</s> class.
And [the affix <s>ṇic</s> is added] in the causative sense (<s>hetumati</s>).
The affix <s>yak</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>kaṇḍvādi</s> group.
The affix <s>āyaḥ</s> [is added] after <s>gupū</s>, <s>dhūpa</s>, <s>vicchi</s>, <s>paṇi</s>, and <s>pani</s>.
The affix <s>īyaṅ</s> [is added] after the root <s>ṛ</s>.
The affix <s>ṇiṅ</s> [is added] after the root <s>kam</s>.
The affixes beginning with <s>āya</s> [are added] optionally when an <s>ārdhadhātuka</s> affix follows.
Stems ending in <s>san</s> and the other [affixes mentioned above] are [called] <s>dhātus</s> (verbal roots).
[The affix <s>sya</s> is added] in the domain of <s>l̥</s> and <s>luṭ</s>, and <s>tāsī</s> [is also added in the domain of <s>luṭ</s>].
The affix <s>sib</s> [is added] variously when a <s>le</s>-replacement [of a <s>lakāra</s>] follows.
The augment <s>ām</s> [is added] after a root ending in a <s>kās</s>-pratyaya, in <s>liṭ</s>, but not in a <s>mantra</s>.
And the <s>ij</s>-substitution [is applied] for a heavy [root], except for <s>ṛccha</s>.
And [the augment <s>ām</s> is added after roots having] <s>daya</s>, <s>aya</s>, and <s>āsa</s> [as substitutes].
Optionally [the augment <s>ām</s> is added] after [the roots] <s>uṣa</s>, <s>vida</s>, and <s>jāgṛ</s>.
And [the augment <s>ām</s> is added after] <s>bhī</s>, <s>hrī</s>, <s>bhṛ</s>, and <s>hu</s>, and [their substitute is] <s>śluvac</s>.
And the root <s>kṛñ</s> is employed as an auxiliary verb in <s>liṭ</s>.
<s>vidāṅ kurvanti</s> — optionally [the periphrastic perfect is formed thus].
<s>abhyutsādayām</s>, <s>prajanayām</s>, <s>cikayām</s>, <s>ramayām akaḥ</s>, <s>pāvayām kriyāt</s>, <s>vidām akran</s> — [these forms occur] in Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>).
The affix <s>cli</s> [is added] in the domain of <s>luḍ</s> (aorist).
[The substitute] <s>sic</s> [replaces] <s>cli</s>.
After a root with an <s>ik</s>-vowel as penultimate and which takes no <s>iṭ</s> augment, [the substitute for <s>cli</s> is] <s>ksa</s>, in place of <s>śal</s> [i.e., the sibilant of <s>sic</s>].
[This rule applies to the root] <s>śliṣ</s> in the sense of embracing.
Not [in the case of] the root <s>dṛś</s>.
After [the roots] <s>ṇi</s>, <s>śri</s>, <s>dru</s>, and <s>sru</s>, [the substitute] <s>caṅ</s> [replaces <s>cli</s>] when the agent is denoted.
Optionally [<s>caṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] after [the roots] <s>dheṭ</s> and <s>śvi</s>.
[<s>caṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] after the root <s>gup</s> in Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>).
Not after [the denominatives] <s>unayati</s>, <s>dhvanayati</s>, <s>elayati</s>, and <s>ardayati</s>.
The affix <s>aṅ</s> [replaces <s>cli</s>] after [the roots denoted by] <s>asyati</s>, <s>vakti</s>, and <s>khyāti</s>.
And after <s>lip</s>, <s>sic</s>, and <s>hve</s>.
Optionally [<s>aṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] in <s>ātmanepada</s> endings.
After roots of the <s>puṣādi</s> group, the <s>dyutādi</s> group, and <s>l̥dit</s> roots, [<s>aṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] in <s>parasmaipada</s> endings.
And after [the roots] <s>sṛ</s>, <s>śās</s>, and <s>ari</s> [<s>aṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s> in <s>parasmaipada</s>].
Optionally after an <s>irit</s> root [<s>aṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>].
And after [the roots] <s>jṝ</s>, <s>stambhu</s>, <s>mrucu</s>, <s>mlucu</s>, <s>grucu</s>, <s>glucu</s>, <s>gluñcu</s>, and <s>śvi</s>.
After [the roots] <s>kṛ</s>, <s>mṛ</s>, <s>dṛ</s>, and <s>ruhi</s> [<s>aṅ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] in Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>).
The affix <s>ciṇ</s> [replaces <s>cli</s> when the endings are those] of the <s>te</s>-series (i.e., <s>ātmanepada</s>) of a <s>pada</s>.
Optionally [<s>ciṇ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] after [the roots] <s>dīp</s>, <s>jan</s>, <s>budh</s>, <s>pūr</s>, <s>tāy</s>, and <s>pyāy</s>.
After a vowel-ending root, [<s>ciṇ</s> replaces <s>cli</s>] in the <s>karmakartari</s> (middle voice with karmic sense).
And after the root <s>duh</s>.
Not after the root <s>rudh</s>.
After the root <s>tap</s>, and also in the sense of <s>anutāpa</s> (remorse).
The affix <s>ciṇ</s> [replaces <s>cli</s>] in <s>bhāva</s> (impersonal) and <s>karman</s> (passive) constructions.
The affix <s>yak</s> [is added] when a <s>sārvadhātuka</s> affix follows.
The affix <s>śap</s> [is added] when the agent is denoted (<s>kartari</s>).
The affix <s>śyan</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>divādi</s> class.
Optionally [<s>śyan</s> is added] after [the roots] <s>bhrāś</s>, <s>bhlāś</s>, <s>bhram</s>, <s>kram</s>, <s>klam</s>, <s>tras</s>, <s>trut</s>, and <s>laṣ</s>.
After the root <s>yas</s> when not preceded by an <s>upasarga</s> (preverb).
And after <s>saṃyas</s> (<s>yas</s> with the preverb <s>sam</s>).
The affix <s>śnu</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>svādi</s> class.
After the root <s>śru</s>, and [the substitute] <s>śṛ</s> [replaces <s>śru</s> before <s>śnu</s>].
After [the root] <s>akṣ</s>, optionally [<s>śnu</s> is added].
After the root <s>takṣ</s> in the sense of making thin.
The affix <s>śa</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>tudādi</s> class.
The affix <s>śnam</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>rudhādi</s> class.
The affix <s>u</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>tanādi</s> class and [the root] <s>kṛñ</s>.
And the vowel <s>a</s> [is substituted] in [the forms] <s>dhinvi</s> and <s>kṛṇvi</s>.
The affix <s>śnā</s> [is added] after roots of the <s>kryādi</s> class.
And the affix <s>śnu</s> [is also added] after [the roots] <s>stambhu</s>, <s>stumbhu</s>, <s>skambhu</s>, <s>skumbhu</s>, and <s>sku</s>.
The <s>śānac</s> and <s>jña</s> [substitutes replace] <s>śna</s> after a consonant.
In Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>), <s>śāyaj</s> also [is used].
Interchange [of affixes] is frequent (<s>bahulam</s>).
The affix <s>aṅ</s> [is added] in <s>liṅ</s> when a benediction (<s>āśis</s>) is expressed.
One who performs an action similar to that of the object is treated like the object (<s>karmavat</s>).
[The word] <s>tapas</s> [is treated as <s>karman</s>] only when the agent of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is the same [as the grammatical subject].
The affixes <s>yak</s> and <s>ciṇ</s> are not [added] after [the roots] <s>duh</s>, <s>snu</s>, and <s>nam</s>.

body.text: kuṣi-rajoḥ prācāṃ śyan parasmaipadaṃ ca || PS_3,1.90 ||
body.translated_text: After [the roots] <s>kuṣ</s> and <s>raj</s>, according to the eastern grammarians, [the affix] <s>śyan</s> [is added] and <s>parasmaipada</s> endings [are used].
[The affixes prescribed in the following rules are added] after a <s>dhātu</s> (verbal root).
In that [rule], the <s>upapada</s> (qualifying word) is [the word] standing in the seventh case (locative).
<s>Kṛt</s> [affixes are those which are added after verbal roots and which are] other than <s>tiṅ</s> (finite verb endings).
Optionally [a <s>kṛt</s> affix is not added] when it would produce a form identical [to the base], except in the feminine.
The <s>kṛtya</s> affixes are [those up to but] before <s>ṇvul</s>.
[The affixes] <s>tavyat</s>, <s>tavya</s>, and <s>anīyar</s> [are added after a verbal root to express obligation].
The affix <s>yat</s> [is added] after a vowel-ending [root].
After [a root ending in a labial consonant, i.e.,] <s>p</s>, with a short vowel as penultimate, [the affix <s>yat</s> is added].
And after [the roots] <s>śak</s> and <s>sah</s>.
And after [the roots] <s>gad</s>, <s>mad</s>, <s>car</s>, and <s>yam</s> when not preceded by an <s>upasarga</s> (preverb).
[The forms] <s>avadya</s>, <s>paṇya</s>, and <s>varya</s> [are irregularly formed with <s>yat</s>] in the senses of 'blameworthy,' 'to be traded,' and 'to be prevented' respectively.
<s>Vahya</s> [with <s>yat</s> denotes] the instrument (a vehicle).
[The form] <s>arya</s> [with <s>yat</s> denotes] a master or a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
[The form] <s>upasaryā</s> [means] a woman suitable for intercourse, and <s>kālyā</s> [means the time] of giving birth.
[The form] <s>ajarya</s> [with <s>yat</s> means] 'well-associated' or 'fitting company.'
After the root <s>vad</s>, when a <s>sup</s> (nominal ending) is in composition, [the affix] <s>kyap</s> [is added] as well.
After the root <s>bhū</s>, [the affix <s>kyap</s> is added] in the sense of <s>bhāva</s> (abstract state).
After the root <s>han</s>, [the affix <s>kyap</s> is added], and [the final of the root is replaced by] <s>t</s>.
The affix <s>kyap</s> [is added] after [the roots] <s>i</s>, <s>stu</s>, <s>śās</s>, <s>vṛ</s>, <s>dṛ</s>, and <s>juṣ</s>.
And after [a root] with <s>ṛ</s> as penultimate, except <s>kl̥p</s> and <s>cṛt</s>.
And [the substitute] <s>ī</s> [replaces the penultimate] of the root <s>khan</s>.
After the root <s>bhṛñ</s>, [the affix <s>kyap</s> is added] when not denoting a proper name.
Optionally after the root <s>mṛj</s> [the affix <s>kyap</s> is added].
[The forms] <s>rājasūya</s>, <s>sūrya</s>, <s>mṛṣodya</s>, <s>rucya</s>, <s>kupya</s>, <s>kṛṣṭapacya</s>, and <s>avyathya</s> [are irregularly formed with <s>kyap</s>].
[The forms] <s>bhidya</s> and <s>uddhya</s> [are formed with <s>kyap</s>] in the sense of a river.
[The forms] <s>puṣya</s> and <s>siddhya</s> [are formed with <s>kyap</s>] in the sense of a <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion).
[The forms] <s>vipūya</s>, <s>vinīya</s>, and <s>jitya</s> [are formed with <s>kyap</s>] in the senses of <s>muñja</s> grass, sediment, and plough respectively.
After the root <s>grah</s> with [the preverbs] <s>prati</s> and <s>api</s>, [the affix <s>kyap</s> is added] in Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>).
And in [the words] <s>pada</s>, <s>asvairi</s>, <s>bāhya</s>, and <s>pakṣya</s>.
Optionally [<s>kyap</s> is added] after the roots <s>kṛ</s> and <s>vṛṣ</s>.
And [the form] <s>yugya</s> [is formed with <s>kyap</s>] in the sense of a leaf.
After [the root forming] <s>amāvasyā</s>, optionally [<s>kyap</s> is added].

In Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>), [the following forms are found with <s>kyap</s>]: <s>niṣṭarkya</s>, <s>devahūya</s>, <s>praṇīya</s>, <s>unnīya</s>, <s>ucchiṣya</s>, <s>marya</s>, <s>starya</s>, <s>dhvarya</s>, <s>khanya</s>, <s>khānya</s>, <s>devayajya</s>, <s>āpṛcchya</s>, <s>pratiṣīvya</s>, <s>brahmavādya</s>, <s>bhāvya</s>, <s>stāvya</s>, <s>upacāyya</s>, and <s>pṛḍa</s>.
The affix <s>ṇyat</s> [is added] after [a root ending in] <s>ṛ</s> or a consonant.
[The affix <s>ṇyat</s> is added] after [a root ending in a vowel belonging to] <s>o</s>, in the sense of necessity.
And after [the roots] <s>āsu</s>, <s>yu</s>, <s>vap</s>, <s>rap</s>, <s>lap</s>, <s>trap</s>, and <s>cam</s>.
[The form] <s>ānāyya</s> [is formed with <s>ṇyat</s>] in the sense of something not permanent.
[The form] <s>praṇāyya</s> [is formed with <s>ṇyat</s>] in the sense of disapproval.
[The forms] <s>pāyya</s>, <s>sānnāyya</s>, <s>nikāyya</s>, and <s>dhāyya</s> [are formed with <s>ṇyat</s>] in the senses of an oblation, a milk offering, a collection, and fuel-verses respectively.
In [the context of] a ritual (<s>kratu</s>), [the forms] <s>kuṇḍapāyya</s> and <s>sañcāyya</s> [are formed with <s>ṇyat</s>].
In [the context of] fire (<s>agni</s>), [the forms] <s>paricāyya</s>, <s>upacāyya</s>, and <s>samūhya</s> [are formed with <s>ṇyat</s>].
And [the forms] <s>citya</s> and <s>agnicitya</s> [are formed with <s>ṇyat</s> in the context of the fire altar].
[The affixes] <s>ṇvul</s> and <s>tṛc</s> [are added after a verbal root to denote the agent].
After [the roots of the] <s>nandi</s>, <s>grahi</s>, and <s>pacādi</s> groups, [the affixes] <s>lyu</s>, <s>ṇini</s>, and <s>ac</s> [are added].
The affix <s>ka</s> [is added] after a root with an <s>ik</s>-vowel as penultimate, and after [the roots] <s>jñā</s>, <s>prī</s>, and <s>kir</s>.
And after [a root ending in] <s>ā</s> when preceded by an <s>upasarga</s> (preverb).
The affix <s>śa</s> [is added] after [the roots] <s>pā</s>, <s>ghrā</s>, <s>dhmā</s>, <s>dheṭ</s>, and <s>dṛś</s>.
And after [the roots] <s>limp</s>, <s>vind</s>, <s>dhār</s>, <s>pār</s>, <s>ved</s>, <s>udej</s>, <s>cet</s>, <s>sāt</s>, and <s>sah</s> when not preceded by an <s>upasarga</s>.
Optionally after [the roots] <s>dadāti</s> and <s>dadhāti</s> [the affix <s>śa</s> is added].
The affix <s>ṇa</s> [is added] after roots [that have forms like] <s>jvaliti</s> and those ending in <s>kas</s>.
And after [the roots] <s>śyā</s>, <s>ād</s>, <s>vyadh</s>, <s>āsru</s>, <s>saṃsṛv</s>, <s>atīṇ</s>, <s>avasā</s>, <s>avahṛ</s>, <s>lih</s>, <s>śliṣ</s>, and <s>śvas</s>.
After [the roots] <s>du</s> and <s>nu</s> when not preceded by an <s>upasarga</s>.
Optionally after the root <s>grah</s> [the affix <s>ṇa</s> is added].
In the sense of a house, [the affix] <s>ka</s> [is added after <s>grah</s>].
In the sense of a craftsman, [the affix] <s>ṣvun</s> [is added].
[The affix] <s>sthakan</s> [is also added in the sense of a craftsman].
And [the affix] <s>ṇyuṭ</s> [is added in the sense of a craftsman].
And [the affix] <s>ha</s> [is added] in the senses of rice and time.
After [the roots] <s>pru</s>, <s>sṛ</s>, and <s>lū</s>, the affix <s>vun</s> [is added] in the sense of repetitive action (<s>samabhihāra</s>).
And [the affix <s>vun</s> is added] in the sense of a benediction (<s>āśis</s>).
The affix <s>aṇ</s> [is added after a verbal root] when the object [is in composition].
And after [the roots] <s>hvā</s>, <s>vā</s>, and <s>am</s> [the affix <s>aṇ</s> is added when the object is in composition].
After [a root ending in] <s>ā</s>, when not preceded by an <s>upasarga</s>, [the affix] <s>ka</s> [is added when the object is in composition].
After the root <s>sthā</s> when a <s>sup</s> (nominal ending) is in composition.
After the roots <s>parimṛj</s> (to wipe off) and <s>apanud</s> (to remove) when <s>tunda</s> (belly) or <s>śoka</s> (grief) is the object.
After the roots <s>dā</s> (to give) and <s>jñā</s> (to know) with the preverb <s>pra</s>.
After the root <s>khyā</s> with the preverb <s>sam</s>.
The affix <s>ṭak</s> [is added] after [the roots] <s>gā</s> and <s>poṣ</s>.
After the root <s>hṛ</s> when not denoting effort, [the affix] <s>ac</s> [is added when the object is in composition].
And [<s>ac</s> is added after <s>hṛ</s>] in the sense of age.
After [a root] with the preverb <s>āṅ</s>, in the sense of habitual action (<s>tācchīlya</s>).
[The affix <s>ac</s> is added after] the root <s>arh</s> [with <s>āṅ</s> in the sense of habitual action].
After the roots <s>ram</s> and <s>jap</s> when <s>stamba</s> (pillar) or <s>karṇa</s> (ear) is the object.
After the root <s>śam</s>, in the sense of a proper name, [the affix is added] when <s>dhātu</s> [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>śī</s> (to lie down) when the sense is a location (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>).
The affix <s>ṭa</s> [is added] after the root <s>car</s>.
And in [the words] <s>bhikṣā</s>, <s>senā</s>, and <s>ādāya</s>.
After the root <s>sṛ</s> when <s>puras</s> (in front), <s>agratas</s> (ahead), or <s>agre</s> (before) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
The preceding [rules apply] when the agent [is in composition].
After the root <s>kṛñ</s> in the senses of cause (<s>hetu</s>), habitual action (<s>tācchīlya</s>), and conformity (<s>ānulomya</s>).

[The affix <s>aṇ</s> is added after <s>kṛñ</s> when the <s>upapada</s> is one of the following:] <s>divā</s>, <s>vibhā</s>, <s>niśā</s>, <s>prabhā</s>, <s>bhāskāra</s>, <s>anta</s>, <s>ananta</s>, <s>ādi</s>, <s>bahu</s>, <s>nāndī</s>, <s>kim</s>, <s>lipi</s>, <s>libi</s>, <s>bali</s>, <s>bhakti</s>, <s>kartṛ</s>, <s>citra</s>, <s>kṣetra</s>, <s>saṅkhyā</s>, <s>jaṅghā</s>, <s>bāhu</s>, <s>ahar</s>, <s>yat</s>, <s>tat</s>, <s>dhanus</s>, and <s>arus</s>.
[The affix <s>aṇ</s> is added] in the sense of the object when wages are involved (<s>bhṛtau</s>).
Not when [the <s>upapada</s> is one of the following:] <s>śabda</s>, <s>śloka</s>, <s>kalaha</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>vaira</s>, <s>cāṭu</s>, <s>sūtra</s>, <s>mantra</s>, or <s>pada</s>.
The affix <s>in</s> [is added] when <s>stamba</s> (tuft) or <s>śakṛt</s> (dung) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>hṛ</s>, when <s>dṛti</s> (leather bag) or <s>nātha</s> (protector) [is the <s>upapada</s>], in the sense of an animal.
And [the forms] <s>phalegrahī</s> and <s>ātmambharī</s> [are formed with the affix <s>in</s>].
In Vedic literature (<s>chandas</s>), [the affix <s>in</s> is added] after [the roots] <s>van</s>, <s>san</s>, <s>rakṣ</s>, and <s>math</s>.
The affix <s>khaś</s> [is added] after the root <s>ej</s>.
After the roots <s>dhmā</s> and <s>dheṭ</s> when <s>nāsikā</s> (nose) or <s>stana</s> (breast) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
And when <s>nāḍī</s> (tube) or <s>muṣṭi</s> (fist) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the roots <s>ruj</s> and <s>vah</s> with the preverb <s>ud</s>, when <s>kūla</s> (bank) is the <s>upapada</s>.
After the root <s>lih</s> when <s>vaha</s> (carrying) or <s>abhra</s> (cloud) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>pac</s> when <s>parimāṇa</s> (measure) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
And when <s>mita</s> (measured) or <s>nakha</s> (nail) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>tud</s> when <s>vidhu</s> (moon) or <s>arus</s> (wound) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>dṛś</s> when <s>asūrya</s> [is the <s>upapada</s>], and after the root <s>tap</s> when <s>lalāṭa</s> (forehead) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
And [the compounds] <s>ugrampaśya</s>, <s>irammada</s>, and <s>pāṇindhama</s> [are irregularly formed].
The affix <s>khac</s> [is added] after the root <s>vad</s> when <s>priyavaśa</s> [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>tāp</s> when <s>dviṣat</s> (enemy) or <s>para</s> (other) [is the <s>upapada</s>].
After the root <s>yam</s> when <s>vāc</s> (speech) [is the <s>upapada</s>], in the sense of a vow.
